sources.entry: What's a senior engineer's job? You need to be more than just an individual contributor.

summary.title: What's a senior engineer's job?
summary.one_liner: A senior engineer's job goes beyond individual programming to include technical helping, quality, project planning and communication, and it helps to set explicit boundaries on what falls outside the role.
keywords: what does a senior engineer do
john allspaw on being a senior engineer
deciding when to stop a project
saying no to work at work
takeaways: A senior engineer's work is mostly technical: writing and reviewing code and design docs, helping stuck teammates, and holding quality standards.
Senior engineers also create new projects, plan and communicate roadmaps, flag risks early, and decide when to stop work.
Tasks like sprint management, 1:1s, team cohesion and fair work allocation are usually a manager's job, though boundaries vary by company.
Agree on expectations explicitly and define a job that is sustainable, enjoyable, and valuable to the team.
Push back on work you can't do or that will make you unhappy long term, since overwork hurts team health.
summary.summary: Julia Evans reflects on John Allspaw's essay "On being a senior engineer" and argues that today the harder question is how to balance leadership work with individual programming. She lists the work she sees as mostly a senior engineer's job, such as code review, helping teammates, creating projects, and proactive risk communication, and separates it from manager tasks like 1:1s and sprint management. The post is a personal, experience-based essay drawn from one company and explicitly offers no definitive answer. It ends with advice on setting boundaries and inviting readers to share how they define their own roles.
